statements.t: Generally, these statements relate to business plans or strategies, projected or anticipated benefits or other consequences of our plans or strategies, projected or anticipated benefits from acquisitions that may be made by us, or projections involving anticipated revenues, earnings or other aspects of our operating results.

The Company entered into an exclusive distribution agreement intended to support the potential commercialization of its SYNC device in Brazil and certain other Latin American markets, subject to applicable regulatory authorizations and other conditions, See “Recent Developments” below.

The Company’s strategy is centered on an integrated technology platform consisting of three complementary components: (i) its proprietary Deep Intracranial Frequency Stimulation (DIFS™) neuromodulation technology, (ii) its HALO™ Clarity device platform, which is being evaluated for physician-supervised home use, and (iii) its Nexalin NeuroCare™ digital health platform, which is intended to support patient…
There can be no assurance that the Company’s clinical trials or regulatory initiatives will be completed within currently anticipated timeframes or result in regulatory authorization.
The acquired software is intended to support the continued development of the Company’s Nexalin NeuroCare™ digital health platform.

We expect the distribution arrangement to support our international commercialization efforts, although the timing and amount of future revenue will depend on regulatory requirements, market demand and the Distributor’s performance.
We expect research and development expenses to fluctuate in future periods based on the timing and scope of clinical trials and continued investment in our digital health software platform.

We expect other income (expense), net, to fluctuate in future periods based on outstanding indebtedness and related financing costs, cash and investment balances, investment activity and prevailing interest rates.

We also expect to continue investing in the integration and development of the Nexalin NeuroCare™ digital health platform, which management believes complements our neuromodulation technologies and supports future commercialization efforts.

The Company expects its working capital to continue to fluctuate based on the timing and level of clinical, regulatory, product development and other operating expenditures; the timing of vendor invoices and payments; and its ability to obtain additional financing.

Our primary uses of capital are, and we expect will continue to be, employee compensation and related expenses; clinical research and development, including our pivotal insomnia clinical trial; development and integration of the Nexalin NeuroCare™ digital health platform; manufacturing and product development; regulatory and quality assurance initiatives; commercialization activities; legal and other professional…
We also expect to use capital to satisfy obligations under our outstanding unsecured promissory note, including required repayments from financing proceeds.

We expect to fund our cash requirements using cash and cash equivalents on hand, and additional financing, including, to the extent available, sales of common stock under our ATM Program and the AMPA.
We expect to continue to incur significant operating losses and negative operating cash flows as we advance our product development, clinical, regulatory and commercialization initiatives.

Management expects continued operating losses and negative operating cash flows as the Company advances its clinical, regulatory, product development and commercialization initiatives, including its pivotal insomnia clinical trial evaluating the HALO™ device, development of the Nexalin NeuroCare™ platform, manufacturing activities and other strategic initiatives.
The Company expects to require additional capital to support its planned operations and strategic initiatives.

After considering the financing activities described above, the related repayments of the Streeterville Promissory Note and management’s other plans, the Company concluded that it does not have sufficient liquidity to fund its anticipated operating requirements for at least twelve months from the date these unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements are issued.
Management intends to seek additional financing, access the ATM Program and the AMPA to the extent available, manage the timing and level of operating expenditures, and pursue revenue opportunities.
The trial is intended to support the Company’s planned De Novo submission to the FDA.
During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, management did not identify any accounting estimates that meet the definition of a critical accounting estimate.

We prepare our unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles, which require our management to make estimates that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities and disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities at the balance sheet dates, as well as the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting periods.

We consider an accounting estimate to be critical if: (i) the accounting estimate requires us to make assumptions about matters that were highly uncertain at the time the accounting estimate was made, and (ii) changes in the estimate that are reasonably likely to occur from period to period or use of different estimates that we reasonably could have used in the current period, would have a material impact on our…
Management does not anticipate a material impact on the Company’s financial position or results of operations from these pronouncements.
